title: Ranking & Seating Arrangement
intro: Two related skills: positional ranking (a person's place from the left/right or top/bottom, and the total count) and seating arrangement (placing people in a row or circle from clues). Ranking is a formula game; arrangement is a drawing game. For both, the cardinal rule is to commit positions to paper and never assume a fact the clues did not give.

items.name: Linear default
items.formula: all face the same way unless stated

topics.name: Order & Ranking
topics.details: When a person's rank is given from both ends, Total = left-rank + right-rank − 1 (the person is counted once in each, so subtract the double count). To convert a rank from one end to the other, use right-rank = Total − left-rank + 1.

topics.name: Linear Arrangement
topics.details: People sit in a single row. Fix the most concrete clue first (someone at an end, or two people adjacent), then add relative clues ('A is to the immediate left of B'). Decide the facing direction — if all face North, 'left' is the arranger's left.

topics.name: Circular Arrangement
topics.details: People sit around a circle, usually facing the centre. When facing the centre, a person's LEFT is the clockwise neighbour and RIGHT is the anticlockwise neighbour — the reverse of intuition.

topics.name: Comparison & Ordering
topics.details: Clues compare heights, ages or marks ('A is taller than B', 'C is shorter than B'). Build a single ordered line from tallest to shortest by chaining the comparisons, then read off who is highest, lowest, or in a given position.

solved.problem: P is older than Q, R is older than P. Oldest?
A > B, C > A. Who is shortest?

unsolved.problem: A > B > C > D. Second tallest?
P < Q, Q < R. Tallest?

X > Y, Z > X. Highest?

shortcuts: Total = left-rank + right-rank − 1 (subtract the double count).
Rank from the other end = Total − rank + 1.
Circle facing centre: left = clockwise, right = anticlockwise.
Chain all comparisons into one ordered line before reading off.
mistakes: Forgetting to subtract 1 in the total-from-two-ranks formula.
Using intuitive left/right in a circle (it flips when facing centre).
Assuming a facing direction the question did not state.
Counting the endpoints when finding "people between".
pyq: SSC asks a ranking-formula item every Tier-1 set and a linear/circular arrangement in Tier 2. The total = L + R − 1 formula alone earns easy marks.
summary: Ranking is formulas: Total = L + R − 1, other-end rank = Total − rank + 1, between = |diff| − 1. Arrangement is drawing: fix the firmest clue first, mind the facing (circle-facing-centre flips left/right), and chain comparisons into one order. Never assume an unstated direction.
